clue.text: Some marshy dragon?

indicators.note: some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run running across the word break

explanation.surface: A question about a dragon that lives in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters across the end of 'marshy' and the start of 'dragon'. The whole clue also describes the beast: the Lernaean monster lived in a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-headed serpent Heracles killed lived in the marshes of Lerna, so it is a swamp-dwelling monster.

clue.text: Homonym confused with earlier power?

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a word that sounds like another muddled up with a former great power?
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' mixes HOMONYM, EARLIER and P. The whole clue then reads as a description: the answer is an earlier power.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval European empire dissolved in 1806 was a power of former times.

clue.text: Pacifists went down quickly in American South

parts.note: in American English the past tense of dive is dove

explanation.surface: Peace campaigners hurried down into the southern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in American' tells you to use the US past tense DOVE rather than British 'dived'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves are people who favour peace over war, the opposite of hawks.

clue.text: Group of blood came in strangely pale

parts.note: A is one of the blood groups

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A blood sample came in looking oddly pallid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges CAME IN to NAEMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anaemic lacks red blood cells and looks pallid and wan.

clue.text: Give delight to EU partner when integrating

indicators.note: integrating means mixing together into one whole, so the letters of the two words are blended and rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomat hopes to please a European Union ally by bringing it closer in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'integrating' is the anagram signal: the nine letters of EU PARTNER are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture is to fill someone with great delight, so it means giving them pleasure.

clue.text: The distant sound of screech-owls

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Faint hooting of owls heard far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' takes the run out of 'screech-owls', spanning the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back, heard faintly and as if from far off.

clue.text: Director of a top company

parts.note: reads as a leading business executive, but the top is the big top of a circus and the company is its troupe

explanation.surface: A senior executive of a leading firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'big top' is the circus tent.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who presents and directs the acts in a circus ring runs its show.

clue.text: Mostly had a good look around dry grassland

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes round another
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pried means looked closely and nosily
to air laundry is to dry it

explanation.surface: Someone scanned the arid grassland closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of the looking word; 'around' wraps the shortened word round the drying word. 'dry' looks like an adjective describing grassland but is the verb, as in drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide treeless stretch of North American plain covered in grasses.

clue.text: This country gets precipitation in surrounding area from Chernobyl

parts.note: for a British newspaper this country is the UK
rain is a form of precipitation

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Britain gets radioactive rain over a wide area after the Chernobyl disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts A inside IN. Chernobyl is in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chernobyl lies in Ukraine, so something from there is Ukrainian by origin.

clue.text: Accommodation .. constructed across the Channel

parts.note: reads like housing built over the sea, but accommodation means an agreement, and this one was made between Britain and France

explanation.surface: Housing built on the far side of the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1904 agreement between Britain and France had a French name.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1904 understanding settling colonial disputes between Britain and France was a friendly agreement.

clue.text: Biblical monster, horribly vile, beheaded prophet

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of vile rearranged give LEVI

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off the word that follows

parts.note: Nathan is the prophet who rebuked King David in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A Bible scene: a monster and a prophet who loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' turns VILE into LEVI; 'beheaded' takes the N off NATHAN to leave ATHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The great sea creature of the Book of Job and the Psalms is a scriptural monster.

clue.text: A piece of poetry about river demon of Muslims

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a fit is an old word for a section of a poem, like a canto

explanation.surface: A verse fragment about a river and a demon from Islamic lore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside FIT to make FRIT, after A. A fit is an archaic term for a division of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabic and Islamic mythology an afreet is a powerful evil jinn, a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Speak again the final section of Stanley's famous words

indicators.note: only the closing part of the quotation is kept, everything before it being dropped

parts.note: the explorer Henry Morton Stanley greeted the missing missionary with 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?'

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to repeat the end of a famous greeting from African exploration.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley's words are 'Dr Livingstone, I presume'; their final section is the end of 'presume' without its P.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin again after a pause, so it covers taking up speaking once more.

clue.text: Poet hugs one coming out

indicators.note: hugs means holds tightly within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American poet and essayist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A poet embraces someone as they emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugs' puts I inside EMERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Emersion is the act of emerging, of rising out of water or reappearing after an eclipse.

clue.text: Latest pair of smuggled items switched for special police — it's a big fiddle

indicators.note: the latest pair are the final two letters of the word
switched for means exchanged, so those letters are replaced by another piece

parts.note: contraband is smuggled goods
the SS was the Nazi special police force

explanation.surface: Smuggled goods are swapped by secret police in a big swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latest pair of' picks the final ND; 'switched for' replaces them with SS. 'fiddle' looks like a fraud but is the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: The double bass, the largest bowed string instrument, is a huge violin-family member.

clue.text: African country caught by notes showing debt that's bad

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A country is said to have been nailed by documents proving bad debts.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU stands for 'I owe you', a written promise to repay.
explanation.definitionFit: Malicious behaviour is spiteful and intended to harm, so it is bad in the moral sense.

clue.text: The opposite of portrait painting

definitions.meaning: in page layout, the wide horizontal orientation as against the tall one

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the wide page orientation and a picture of rural scenery.

clue.text: Cut off cover in vehicle insurance terminations

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
terminations are ends, so the last letter of each of the two words is taken

parts.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box

explanation.surface: Car insurance cover is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminations' gives E and E, the last letters of 'vehicle' and 'insurance'; 'in' puts LID between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit a sound or syllable when speaking, cutting it off.

clue.text: A day in Rome with new cardinals

parts.note: cardinal numbers are counting numbers such as one, so ones are cardinals

explanation.surface: A day in Rome spent with newly appointed cardinals of the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' looks like the Vatican's princes of the Church, but it means cardinal numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient Roman calendar the nones fell on the seventh or ninth day of each month.

clue.text: Financial restriction to constrain press

definitions.meaning: a credit ... is a tightening of borrowing

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a credit crunch, forcing into tight limits, and compressing something.

clue.text: Time to enclose explosive control so as to penetrate identified location

definitions.text: so as to penetrate identified location

indicators.note: to enclose means to surround, so the outer pieces wrap round the inner ones

parts.note: taken as written
HE stands for high explosive
a rein is a strap used to control a horse, so to rein is to control

explanation.surface: Bomb disposal: time is short to contain an explosive device before getting into the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to' supplies the two outer pieces and 'enclose' wraps them round the bomb and the control; HE is the usual crossword shorthand for high explosive. The definition is a stiff paraphrase of an old legal adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereinto is a formal adverb meaning into that place or thing already mentioned.

clue.text: Service gets in three points all together

indicators.note: gets in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: E, N and E are three compass points
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A church service gets in three points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts MASS inside E, N, E.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for in a body, everyone at once.

clue.text: Like tongue with some beef?

parts.note: the surface suggests a cold cut of tongue alongside roast beef, but tongue is an organ made of muscle and beef is slang for brawn

explanation.surface: A deli order: tongue served alongside some beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' as slang means muscle power, and the tongue is itself a muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brawny and built of muscle tissue, as the tongue is, fits this adjective.

clue.text: Mischievous boy takes aim to threaten

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
an end is an aim or goal, as in 'ends and means'

explanation.surface: A naughty boy takes aim as if to menace someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to loom or hang over menacingly, as danger does.

clue.text: Strangely in tune, but out of time, which is boring

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters are rearranged, with one taken out

explanation.surface: Music played in tune but out of time is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T from IN TUNE and rearrange; 'but out of' signals the removal. 'which is boring' reads as an adjective, but the answer is the noun 'what is boring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, the tedium of something dull.

clue.text: Runs and makes purchase of audio system?

indicators.note: an audio system is what you hear, so the word is taken as heard, not as written

parts.note: to buy is to make a purchase

explanation.surface: Someone runs off and buys a hi-fi.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket byes are runs scored when the ball passes the batter and keeper without being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes are extras in cricket, counted towards the batting side's total of runs.

clue.text: Buccaneer deprived of power is incensed

indicators.note: deprived of means having something taken away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a buccaneer is a pirate

explanation.surface: A pirate stripped of his authority is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' takes P away from PIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, which is what incensed means.

clue.text: Getting deep into one area, here in Africa, once?

parts.note: the deep is an abyss, a bottomless chasm
into gives IN
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone gets deep into a region of Africa, asking whether it was once called something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the definition is by example: the country is now Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the former name of Ethiopia, a country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Soccer teams with energy getting second break

parts.note: a football side has eleven players, so teams are elevens

explanation.surface: Football teams with energy get a second half after the break.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack, taken around eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a short mid-morning pause for tea and a biscuit, a kind of rest.

clue.text: Pick priest depicted by heartless Trollope

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

indicators.note: heartless means with the middle removed, so only the first and last letters of the name stay

explanation.surface: Choosing a clergyman as portrayed by the novelist Anthony Trollope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves T and E, the first and last letters of 'Trollope'. Trollope wrote novels about clergy, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, the pick of the bunch.
